findings.title: SEED-02 root cause: contamination guard is a negative allowlist of REGISTERED sibling projects — unregistered foreign work (Salesforce/FastMCP) is invisible, and the 'claude' identity keyword makes the fallback structurally unable to protect a project named continuous-claude
causal_links: D2d-02 (selection layer that fed the guard the foreign plan)
caused SEED-02

evidence.quote: the `post-plan-roadmap` hook clobbered this Current Focus with a foreign project's goal (Salesforce/FastMCP plan `abstract-coral`) — the cross-project contamination guard did not catch it

findings.observe_how: Verified event reconstruction: ~/.claude/plans/we-have-been-working-abstract-coral.md mtime = 2026-06-05 19:55:49 -0500 (= 2026-06-06T00:55 UTC), which matches the contaminated entry's UTC-stamped date '### 2026-06-06: Harden the Alpha...' and 'Started: 2026-06-06' (post-plan-roadmap.ts:587 uses toISOString UTC date). The clobber fired ~19:55 local on 06-05 (foreign plan freshly written, so the 10-min staleness guard passed it LEGITIMATELY); contaminated ROADMAP was committed unnoticed in 137ec87 (06-06 08:34) and restored in 8201551 (09:59). The guard missed for two independent reasons, both verified: (1) isContentRelevantToProject only flags content that names another REGISTERED project — the registry holds only continuous-claude/NorthStar/Fourth Connect/agent-factory/ECG/LinkMap, so a Salesforce/FastMCP plan (7x 'salesforce', 0 registry names) hits the fail-open 'no cross-project signals' path; (2) even if a salesforce project WERE registered, the abstract-coral plan contains 'claude' 3x (CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/plans path), and 'claude' is an identity keyword of continuous-claude (dirName split), so contentLower.includes('claude') would set thisProjectMentioned=true and pass it anyway. Any plan authored under Claude Code mentions 'claude' — the keyword fallback can never protect this repo. Fix direction: positive relevance check against THIS project (not a sibling allowlist), word-boundary matching, and excluding ecosystem-universal tokens ('claude','continuous') from identity keywords.
findings.telemetry: 1 confirmed S0 contamination event (2026-06-06); same fail-open path returns 'relevant' for every unregistered-foreign plan, so recurrence probability is high whenever foreign work is planned from this repo's cwd

findings.title: post-plan-roadmap plan selection reads newest-mtime .md from the machine-global shared ~/.claude/plans pool and ignores the firing event's own tool_input.plan; the tool_output/tool_result fallback uses non-canonical field names
causal_links: feeds D2d-01 (gave the guard the foreign plan content)
D2d-12 (field-name drift instance)
findings.observe_how: This repo has NO local .claude/plans or ./plans (verified by ls), so planDir always resolves to the global ~/.claude/plans — a directory shared by ALL projects' sessions (verified: it contains both this repo's starry-pony plan and the foreign abstract-coral plan). Selection is newest-mtime-within-10-min with zero session/plan binding, so a concurrent terminal planning another project can win the race and have ITS plan recorded into this repo's ROADMAP — the 10-minute 'staleness' window defends against old files, not against fresh foreign ones (the actual threat in SEED-02). The authoritative content — tool_input.plan, the plan markdown of the very ExitPlanMode that fired the hook (its existence proven by sibling hook plan-exit-premortem-prompt reading toolInput.plan) — is never consulted; the only non-disk fallback reads data.tool_output/data.tool_result, neither of which is the canonical PostToolUse field (shared/types.ts declares tool_response). Bonus amplifier: sessions are keyed by UTC date and same-day entries are REPLACED, so a foreign plan landing on the same UTC date silently overwrites the legit session record (exactly what 8201551 had to restore).
findings.telemetry: 8 plan files currently in the shared global pool from multiple projects; any two sessions exiting plan mode within 10 minutes of each other are in the race window

findings.title: epistemic-reminder is dead code in production: reads input.tool (canonical field is tool_name) so the Grep match never fires — yet claim-verification.md tells every session the hook 'injects warnings after Grep results'
causal_links: D2d-12 (field-name drift instance)

evidence.quote: The `epistemic-reminder` hook injects warnings after Grep results. Follow them.

findings.observe_how: Registered live with matcher Grep|Read (verified in ~/.claude/settings.json), so it spawns a node process on EVERY Grep and Read, then always prints '{}' because input.tool is undefined (Claude Code sends tool_name; every other hook in src/ uses tool_name). Even if the field matched, the output uses systemPromptSuffix — not the additionalContext field the repo's own hook-dev-lifecycle rule documents as 'the reliable inject pattern'. Double-dead, plus a decision-driving false claim in a rule loaded into every session's context. Fix is two field renames, or delete the hook and the rule's enforcement sentence.
findings.telemetry: Fires on every Grep/Read tool call session-wide; injected reminders delivered: 0

findings.title: ralph-monitor is dead code: gates on data.event !== 'PostToolUse' but the harness sends hook_event_name (and it reads tool_result, not tool_response) — exits instantly on every Bash call it spawns for
causal_links: D2d-12 (field-name drift instance)
D2d-05 (the compensating Task-side monitor is also field-broken — Ralph hook-side state updates are entirely dead)

evidence.quote:
const stdout = data.tool_result?.stdout || '';
        const stderr = data.tool_result?.stderr || '';
* This creates the feedback loop from Ralph containers back to Maestro orchestration.

findings.observe_how: Registered live on PostToolUse matcher=Bash (verified in ~/.claude/settings.json). The harness input carries hook_event_name (the convention 8+ sibling hooks in src/ use — arch-context-inject, memory-awareness, compiler-in-the-loop, etc.); 'event' is never present, so the guard at line 233 makes the hook exit(0) on every single invocation before any signal parsing. Even with that fixed, stdout/stderr are read from tool_result while the canonical field is tool_response (shared/types.ts). Net effect: the documented 'feedback loop from Ralph containers back to Maestro' has never functioned; the hook is pure per-Bash-call process-spawn overhead. Fix the two field names or delete and rely on ralph-task-monitor (after D2d-05 is fixed).
findings.telemetry: One wasted node spawn per Bash tool call session-wide; Ralph signals processed: 0

findings.title: ralph-task-monitor never sees agent output in production: reads input.tool_result.{stdout,content,text} while the harness delivers tool_response — resultText is always empty and all three detection tiers are unreachable
causal_links: D2d-12 (field-name drift instance)
with D2d-04, both Ralph hook-side task-state updaters are dead — explains reliance on manual ralph-checkpoint/state edits
findings.observe_how: Same event, same matcher (PostToolUse matcher=Agent, verified registered): sibling hook agent-error-capture reads input.tool_response; ralph-task-monitor reads input.tool_result. Both cannot be right. shared/types.ts declares tool_response as the canonical PostToolUseInput field. With tool_result absent, resultText is '' and the hook returns at line 327 before structured-JSON/XML/pattern detection or any Braintrust agent_task_success emit — so during live Ralph runs, agent completions never auto-update .ralph/state.json from the Task path. Unit tests pass because they feed tool_result directly (test-only contract). Observe by running a Ralph session and checking that no 'RALPH TASK MONITOR:' additionalContext ever appears after Task completions.
findings.telemetry: agent_task_success Braintrust emits from this hook: effectively 0 in production; corr-null 60.7% and 30/36 agents never in agent-recall are consistent with Task-side PostToolUse consumers not seeing payloads

findings.title: agent-error-capture (and hook-error-pipeline) shell out to store_learning.py via execSync string concatenation with only quote/newline escaping — on Windows cmd.exe, error content containing \" or metachars breaks quoting; this is the junk-file creation mechanism family of SEED-01
causal_links: candidate mechanism for SEED-01 junk artifacts
D2d-07 (over-broad triggers raise how often hostile content reaches this shell path)
findings.observe_how: The content fed to --content is raw agent error output (stack traces, code snippets) which routinely contains ", >, &, |, ^ and %. Escaping handles only " and newline; on Windows, execSync runs via cmd.exe where backslash-escaped quotes do not reliably keep cmd's own quote state — a " in content toggles quoting and any following > or & becomes live redirection/chaining, creating stray files in cwd (opcDir = opc/) — matching the SEED-01 artifact location ('junk files under opc/', also recorded at ROADMAP.md:197 finding (a)). The codebase already has the safe pattern in the SAME file family: post-plan-roadmap, smarter-everyday, periodic-extract and browser-learning-extractor all use spawn with an args ARRAY (no shell). Fix: convert agent-error-capture.ts:176 and hook-error-pipeline.ts:103 to spawnSync('uv', [args...]). Note: SEED-01's daily ~07:24 writer still needs the Task-Scheduler probe — these two hooks are event-driven, so they are the mechanism family, not necessarily the scheduled invoker.
findings.telemetry: SEED-01 reports 5 junk artifacts to date; ROADMAP.md:197 records one regenerated mid-session on 2026-06-06

findings.title: agent-error-capture stores FAILED_APPROACH memories on /\berror\b/ alone — successful agent runs that merely mention 'error' ('0 errors', 'error handling') are recorded as failures, polluting archival_memory recall; store is also a synchronous execSync (up to 10s) in the Task hot path
causal_links: contributes to memory-recall hit-rate 27.4% (false FAILED_APPROACH entries dilute recall)
D2d-06 (each false trigger also exercises the unsafe shell path)

evidence.quote:
if (hasError) {
      // Only store on actual error patterns (TypeError, ENOENT, etc.)

findings.observe_how: The comment at line 223 claims storage happens 'only on actual error patterns (TypeError, ENOENT, etc.)' but ERROR_PATTERNS leads with bare /\berror\b/i, /\bfailed\b/i, /\bfailure\b/i, /\btimeout\b/i — words present in most healthy agent reports ('all tests passed, 0 errors', 'added error handling'). The G3 quality scorer drops NOISE (<3) but BORDERLINE (3-4) passes, so plausible-looking false failures land tagged agent_failure/FAILED_APPROACH. Query archival_memory for tags LIKE '%agent_failure%' and sample: entries quoting success summaries confirm. Separately, the store is execSync with a 10s ceiling inside PostToolUse:Agent — every false positive adds seconds of blocking latency after agent completion (cf. SEED-16's same store-hot-path pattern). Fix: drop the bare error/failed/failure/timeout words (keep stack-trace and errno patterns), and use detached spawn like post-plan-roadmap does.
findings.telemetry: memory-recall hit-rate 27.4%; every Task completion whose text contains 'error' pays the scorer + possible 10s execSync

findings.title: agent-verification delivers its entire output (the verification warning) via the legacy top-level 'message' field that the repo's own types/docs mark deprecated — warnings likely never reach Claude, making the hook decorative
causal_links: D2d-12 (output-contract drift sibling)

evidence.quote: - Context injection: `PostToolUse additionalContext` is the reliable inject pattern

findings.observe_how: The hook's sole purpose is injecting '⚠️ AGENT VERIFICATION WARNING' context after suspicious agent claims, but it never uses hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext — only { message }, which shared/types.ts labels legacy/deprecated and hook-dev-lifecycle.md contrasts with the 'reliable inject pattern'. Sibling hooks on the same event (ralph-task-monitor, post-plan-roadmap) all wrap context in hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. Secondary nit: the existsSync check at lines 146-151 tests bare filenames ('!file.includes("/")') relative to the hook process cwd, generating false 'files that don't exist' warnings for valid relative paths — low-stakes only because the channel is dead. Observe: trigger a kraken/spark response claiming completion without files and check that no warning appears in context. Fix: route warnings through additionalContext (one-function change).
findings.telemetry: Registered on PostToolUse matcher=Agent; warning deliveries observable in transcripts: none expected via legacy field

findings.title: prd-roadmap-sync marks the CURRENT ROADMAP goal complete whenever ANY fully-checked tasks-*.md is written — titleToComplete falls back to roadmap.current.title with no check that the tasks file relates to the current goal; section matching is first-word substring
causal_links: same unguarded-ROADMAP-write family that roadmap-completion already had to neuter (its lines 150-152 document the prior clobber)
findings.observe_how: Write any tasks-foo.md inside the project with all checkboxes ticked: handleTasksChange computes isComplete=true and calls moveToCompleted(roadmapContent, roadmap.current?.title) — the CURRENT goal, even if 'foo' is unrelated to it — replacing Current Focus with the '_No current goal._' placeholder and appending a bogus '- [x]' line. moveToCompleted/promoteToCurrent/updateProgress all match sections by the FIRST WORD of the title via substring includes (line 335), so titles sharing a first word ('CCv3-Hardening ...') cross-match. roadmap-completion was already converted to advisory-only after exactly this clobbering failure mode (its own comment is the precedent), but prd-roadmap-sync retained the unconditional fs.writeFileSync path. Fix: require the tasks file's featureName to match the current goal before completing, or convert to advisory like roadmap-completion.
findings.telemetry: Registered live on Write|Edit; trigger frequency tied to ai-dev-tasks usage (tasks-*.md files)

findings.title: git-commit-roadmap records commits into THIS project's ROADMAP without verifying the commit ran in this project — 'cd <other-repo> && git commit' (routine for ~/.claude quick fixes) writes a foreign repo's commit into the session project's Completed section
causal_links: second cross-project ROADMAP contamination vector alongside SEED-02/D2d-01 (different hook, same class)

evidence.quote:
const projectDir = process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || process.cwd();
  const roadmapPath = findRoadmapPath(projectDir);

findings.observe_how: The Bash command string is only checked for the substring 'git commit'; nothing inspects a leading 'cd <path> &&' or compares the commit's repo to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. The git-sync workflow in this environment explicitly commits in OTHER directories from a session ('cd ~/continuous-claude && git commit' from any project, ~/.claude quick fixes) — each such feat:/fix: commit appends a '- [x]' entry to the CURRENT session project's ROADMAP Completed with today's date and the foreign hash. Reproduce: from a session in project A, run cd ../project-B && git commit -m 'feat: x' and read project A's ROADMAP. Fix: parse a leading cd target (or run git -C check) and skip when the commit repo differs from projectDir.
findings.telemetry: Registered live on PostToolUse:Bash; cross-repo commits are a documented routine pattern in git-sync-workflow.md

findings.title: smarter-everyday reads Bash output as tool_response.output ONLY — if the harness delivers stdout/stderr, test success/failure is never detected, the state machine dead-ends in TESTING, and the entire 'victory library' silently captures nothing
causal_links: D2d-12 (Bash-payload field drift instance)
if dead, contributes to low WORKING_SOLUTION density behind memory-recall hit-rate 27.4%

evidence.quote: const output = String((toolResponse as { output?: string })?.output || '');

findings.observe_how: Sibling hook git-commit-roadmap defends against BOTH Bash payload shapes (.output then .stdout); smarter-everyday and roadmap-completion's handleBashOutput read .output only. If the runtime delivers {stdout,stderr}, output is '' so isTestSuccess/isTestFailure both return false; the machine transitions ATTEMPTING→TESTING and TESTING has no outbound transitions anywhere in processTransition (CANDIDATE is only reachable from ATTEMPTING with detected success), so no victory is ever stored. Cheap observation: query archival_memory for tags LIKE '%victory%' — zero rows since deployment confirms the dead-end; any rows disconfirm. Also doc drift: header says state lives at .claude/smarter-everyday-state.json but getStateFilePath returns getSessionStatePath('smarter-everyday') (temp dir). Fix: read output || stdout (+stderr) like git-commit-roadmap, and add a TESTING fallback transition.
findings.telemetry: Registered on Edit|Write|Bash|TaskUpdate (4-tool matcher = high fire rate) — full state-file read/write cycle per event even while the victory path may be unreachable

findings.title: Structural: PostToolUse input/output contract drift across the 13 hooks — five competing field spellings (tool vs tool_name, event vs hook_event_name, tool_result vs tool_response vs tool_output, .output vs .stdout, message vs additionalContext) with no shared input normalizer; 4+ hooks silently dead or degraded as a result
causal_links: parent of D2d-03 (tool), D2d-04 (event/tool_result), D2d-05 (tool_result), D2d-08 (message), D2d-11 (.output); partial parent of D2d-02 (tool_output)
findings.observe_how: shared/types.ts already defines the canonical PostToolUseInput (tool_name + tool_response), yet each hook re-declares its own ad-hoc input interface, and the wrong spellings type-check fine because the fields are optional. Concretely broken today: epistemic-reminder (tool), ralph-monitor (event + tool_result), ralph-task-monitor (tool_result), post-plan-roadmap (tool_output/tool_result fallback), smarter-everyday + roadmap-completion (.output-only Bash payload), agent-verification (message-only output). One shared parseHookInput()/bashOutputOf() helper in shared/ (mirroring the existing atomic-write/session-isolation helpers) plus deleting per-hook input interfaces eliminates the whole bug class and makes the 35/111-unregistered audit meaningful (a registered hook would actually run). Leverage: this is why several hooks pass their unit tests (tests feed the hook's own invented shape) while being dead in production.
findings.telemetry: 4 hooks verified dead/degraded by this class in D2d alone; 111 hook srcs share the copy-paste input pattern

findings.title: prd-roadmap-sync path containment uses startsWith prefix comparison — sibling dirs sharing the prefix (continuous-claude-x) bypass the guard; one-line path.relative fix
causal_links: D2d-09 (same hook's write path makes the weak guard matter)
findings.observe_how: Payoff: replacing with a path.relative(projectDir, filePath) '..'-check closes both the sibling-prefix bypass (C:\...\continuous-claude-evil passes for projectDir C:\...\continuous-claude) and Windows drive-letter case mismatch false rejections — the same bug class the Codex adversary caught in the Phase A bus code.

notes: All 13 assigned hooks read in full at the frozen working tree; registration cross-checked in both repo and active settings.json (all 13 registered live; plan-exit-premortem-prompt active-only = SEED-15 instance). SEED-02 prize delivered with timestamped reconstruction: foreign plan abstract-coral written to the shared global ~/.claude/plans at 2026-06-05 19:55:49 -0500; hook fired in a continuous-claude-cwd session within the 10-min freshness window (so the staleness guard passed it legitimately — it defends the wrong threat); UTC date stamping explains the '2026-06-06' labels; contamination committed unnoticed in 137ec87 (06-06 08:34) and restored in 8201551 (09:59). Guard missed for two independent verified reasons: registry-negative-allowlist (Salesforce/FastMCP not registered) and 'claude'-keyword poisoning (the fallback can never protect a project literally named continuous-claude).
